source_text: Right, and then this raises an interesting question about the 6 hour gap, which I think is still a good number but probably shouldn't be hard-coded if we want the system to be maximally useful, because e.g. with the solve-loop it is totally automated even if I do sit around reading logs.  A gap-time=0 would just show a continuous decomposition of token usage over time, I guess; a gap-time=1 might be interesting to show things that have been running autonomously while I go shopping or something rather than overnight / on a long flight / etc.

reply_text:
The code is right and my test was wrong: the second stretch is exactly 1 hour long, so a 1-hour threshold includes it. I'll shorten that stretch in the test.Gist: The gap length is now a setting, `--gap-hours`, with 6 as the default. At 1 hour it picks up errands, and at 0 it shows how all agent tokens were spread across the stretches between turns you typed. The new download and its checksum are committed in futon7a but not pushed, so futon7a is now two commits ahead of the live site, together with the earlier gap-chart commit.

I ran both new settings on your last 12 hours:

- **`--gap-hours 1`:** one gap, 05:27 to 13:15, which is 7.8 hours with 2.2 million tokens.
- **`--gap-hours 0`:** 38 stretches between typed turns, holding 90% of the 748 million tokens logged. The biggest was 107 million tokens in the 34 minutes from 02:42 to 03:16. The other 10% of tokens fall before your first typed turn or after your last one in the window, so no stretch contains them.

Both sample reports are on staging, at `/staging/xiaoxiang-sample-report-gap1.html` and `/staging/xiaoxiang-sample-report-gap0.html`. The chart caption and the terminal summary change their wording to match the setting. At 0, for example, they say "stretch between turns you typed" instead of "gap of at least N hours".

One limit: the setting doesn't solve the solve-loop problem you described. The tool can only see when you typed, so an hour spent reading logs still counts as a gap. At 0 that doesn't matter, because the chart just shows where the tokens went over time. But no threshold separates "watching" from "away".

The box on the site still shows `--days 7` with the default. I haven't mentioned the new option there, so you can decide whether it belongs in the box. `python3 xiaoxiang-local.py --help` describes it.

**Tests:** all three test files pass. The new test runs the same turns and tokens with thresholds of 6, 1 and 0 and checks which stretches each one keeps. My first version of that test was wrong: it used a stretch of exactly 1 hour, which a 1-hour threshold correctly includes. The code was right, and I fixed the test.

**Commits:** futon3c 53beb3da, futon7 cc63f2f, futon7a 7d1adfe.
